nom: The Ordinary Resveratrol 3% + Ferulic Acid 3% Antioxidant Serum for Brightening

segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin describe the serum as hydrating, velvety and plumping, though a few say their driest patches never fully absorb it and are left with a shiny, non-matte film they prefer to apply only at night.
segments.oily: Reviewers with oily skin report it works when used in the evening only, leaving skin smooth without visible shine, though the serum's own oily finish leads some non-oily reviewers to doubt it would suit very oily or humid-climate skin.
segments.combination: Reviewers with combination skin describe an initial oily feel that settles into a soft, mattified finish within seconds, with their skin behaving oilier in summer and drier in winter.
segments.sensitive: Many reviewers with sensitive skin, including some who are rosacea-prone or reactive, report no stinging, redness or breakouts and even calmer skin, but a substantial number of other reviewers, some explicitly saying they are not normally sensitive, describe severe burning, swelling or allergic-type reactions to the same product.
segments.mature: Reviewers in their 40s to 60s report brighter, firmer-looking skin and visibly softened fine lines and wrinkles with regular use, and several defend the product against burning complaints as a sign of a weak skin barrier rather than a flaw in the serum.

concerns.aging: Reviewers focused on aging report smoother texture, smaller-looking pores and softened fine lines, including a 50-year-old who noticed forehead wrinkles visibly lighter and a 39-year-old esthetician who rates its effect on par with professional anti-aging products.
concerns.dehydration: Reviewers dealing with dryness generally report plumper, more moisturized skin after regular use, though a couple note it leaves a heavy or shiny film that their driest patches never fully absorb.
concerns.redness: One reviewer with sensitive, redness-prone skin reports it calmed and evened her complexion, which contrasts with a larger group of reviewers who describe the product itself triggering new redness, swelling or a burning sensation.
concerns.barrier: Several reviewers argue the burning some people experience signals a compromised skin barrier rather than a problem with the product, and one reviewer found it stopped working well once her barrier grew more reactive after pregnancy, regaining effectiveness only after her skin calmed down.
concerns.spots: Reviewers using it for dark spots, melasma or post-acne hyperpigmentation report fading and brightening over weeks to months, though one reviewer with acne and hyperpigmentation saw no noticeable improvement.
concerns.blemishes: Several reviewers report fewer breakouts and reduced cystic acne, including fading scars and calmer hormonal breakouts, but this contrasts with other reviewers who developed new acne spots or congested, clogged pores within days of starting the product.
concerns.oiliness: One reviewer with combination skin says the serum mattifies after absorbing for a few seconds, but many other reviewers describe a persistently oily or greasy finish that some feel would add unwanted shine for oil-prone skin.

aspects.libelle: Risk of burning or allergic reaction
Unusual scent, likened to campfire or rubber
Helps sunscreen glide on without pilling
A little goes a long way, bottle lasts

extraits.texte: I use so many of The Ordinary products and I love them. This particular one though did not love me. I'm 51 and always trying new things in skincare. For months, I could not figure out which product was causing this as I had a bottle of oils mixed with my favorite carrier oils and the resveritrol in there as well. To a lesser degree than the picture I will post, it happened when I'd use the mixture. I gave up on the whole bottle. The other night I was going to bed and decided I'd use the resveritrol alone. It had a warming effect on my skin and I went to bed. I woke up to what you see in the picture. My eyes were swollen so badly. The redness, the burning feeling is awful. At least now I know what it was in the mixture I made that caused it because I used the resveritrol alone and woke to this. A steroid cream, hydrocortisone, Benedryl and slathering in Aquaphor, 3 days later it's still red but getting better.

This product was a total disaster for me. Within just three days of using it, my cheeks and forehead were covered in acne spots and the skin around my nose was dry and flaky. Also the fine lines under my eyes seemed bigger than usual because of skin dryness. I took a break from using it for two weeks to get my face back to normal, but when I gave it another try, the same thing happened all over again. I sure won't be using it again.

extraits.titre: Helps sunscreen blend, no noticeable skin benefits
extraits.texte: I have been using this for 4 months. A little goes a long way- 3 drops for face and neck Light weight oil texture- comfortable and sinks in quickly. I do not notice any smell The best thing about this formula is that it stops my sunscreen pilling completely and makes sunscreen melt into skin quickly and more seamlessly. I have acne and hyperpigmentation, I have seen no noticeable improvement with this so far. I will be repurchasing for antioxidant support and for better sunscreen application and wear.

I've been trying to figure out the perfect anti-aging regimen for my skin so I've been experimenting with lots of The Ordinary products over the past year. I have to say that this is one of my favorites!! My skin is very dry so i'm always looking for products that help moisturize without being too oily. This stuff makes my feel so hydrated and almost velvety. I use morning and night after putting on my other products. My morning routine = Marine Hyaluronics, Lactic Acid 5%, The Buffet...followed by a few drops Resveratrol & Ferulic Acid - which I let sink in for a few minutes then I finish up with Cera Ve cream. Night routine = Tretenoin followed up with a few drops Resveratrol & Ferulic Acid - which I let sink in for a few minutes then I finish up with Cera Ve cream. I've only been using for a few weeks and I feel that my skin texture had improved. My pores look smaller and overall I look more moisturized / dewy. I think it's important to remember that a little bit goes a long way with this product. I could see using too much as being too oily. I only use 3-4 small drops for my face and neck area each time. If you have dry skin I'd definitely recommend giving this a try!

I tried this a couple years ago and didn't notice great effects but I take resveratrol orally and *have* noticed good effects so I gave it another try. This time I followed the label carefully. I apply a small amount after water based treatments, before heavy oils and moisturizer, twice per day. Just 1-2 drops for the whole face. This, in combination w several products (incl GF from TO) has produced noticable improvements in pore size/texture, elasticity, clarity, and reduction in wrinkle depth. In 2 months it's taken years off my face, and it was the only thing I changed before adding GF a week ago. I was slathering this on by itself and I think it didn't absorb properly. PLUS the nmn and nac cream, peptides, and HA I use also help but they weren't doing much until I added this. The smell is like rubber bands but faint and dissipates quickly. I am 46, with very fair, dry, sensitive skin prone to rosacea.

extraits.titre: Great alternative to Kiel's Ferulic Acid toner!
extraits.texte: Are you kidding me? I've already purchased this twice. I got this as a replacement to a kiehl's lactic acid and ferulic acid toner, and its amazing. I usually alternate this with the 10% lactic acid from TO and my skin texture has become so smooth. I still get the occasional hormonal acne or if I'm not drinking enough water, but I use this at night and my pimple is very much reduced in the morning. I also have combo skin, in the summers its oily but in the winter it gets kinda dry. I probably wouldn't have tried it if it wasn't for the expensive one that I didn't want to purchase, but this actually turned out to be a great alternative. This is a must try if you want hydration but also clearer skin. I don't think I would recommend this to people with oily skin since this is a very oily serum.

extraits.titre: AMAZING...but ONLY if your skin barrier is healthy
extraits.texte: I used this product morning and night (1-2 drops) consistently for ~2 years with amazing results. Noticeably brightened my skin with the added bonus of a low price point and one bottle lasting for ages. However, after having a baby, my skin became more sensitive, and this product couldn't do its job under those conditions. It took me a good 6 months to realize that I should change my skincare routine, and at that point, I saw that my skin was less irritated when I didn't use this product (the primary culprit, however, was over-exfoliation). I tried to re-introduce this product around a year after changing my skincare routine, but it didn't seem to have much effect. However, when I recently re-introduced it again (I now have melasma and it's driving me nuts!), I noticed that my skin was responding positively right away. So bottom line: this product is absolutely AMAZING, BUT your skin barrier must be healthy enough to benefit. If this product doesn't work for you, or you suddenly can't tolerate it after a long period of use, consider a gentler skincare regimen and then try re-introducing it later; it's definitely worth trying because my skin hasn't been as bright without this product. I am SO happy that I can use it again!
